newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Irish President retires Sept 12 to take up U.N. post.
newsitem.headline: Irish President retires Sept 12 to take up U.N. post.

text.p: Ireland's President Mary Robinson announced on Thursday she would step down as head of state on September 12, nearly three months before the end of her term, to take up her new post as the top U.N. human rights official.
"I will retire from the presidency of Ireland on September 12 September at 1 pm," she told reporters, with Secretary-General Kofi Annan standing beside her.

Robinson was approved by the U.N. General Assembly on June 17 as the next U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights. But the date for the start of her four-year term in the Geneva-based post was left open.
Annan has been anxious for her to take over before the beginning of the annual General Assembly session opening on September 16.
Robinson, 53, is a lawyer and human rights legal expert, as well as the first woman elected president of Ireland. Her seven-year term as head of state would normally end on December 2.
"I have understood from the secretary-general that he has been very anxious to have me on board and to know the date when I would assume the post of High Commissioner," she said.
"And I have indicated to him that I will retire from the presidency of Ireland on 12th of December, at 1 pm. And I will then be in a position to take up the post," she said, misstating the month.

After Annan whispered in her left ear, she quickly corrected herself, saying: "12th of September, at 1 o'clock. And I would hope then to go to Geneva and then to come to New York in time for the General Assembly's 52nd session," she added.

In introducing Robinson, Annan said: "We are excited to have her on board. We think she is going to be a wonderful addition to the team. I was going to use the word 'superstar' but I didn't want to embarrass her."
Robinson thanked Annan and said she was honoured to have been nominated by him and approved by the General Assembly.

She said it was a daunting task but a very important one that "fits in well with the thinking of the secretary-general ... in the reform of the U.N. itself and its purposes. It is for the purpose of the principles of the United Nations and at the heart of that is human rights throughout the world."
She told a questioner that she and Annan also discussed the post of her future deputy. She said she had asked for a little more time to consider potential candidates and the nature of the office.
"I am certainly very aware of the importance of having good geographical balance, a good sense of bringing together North and South in a joint commitment to human rights," she said.

Robinson will succeed Jose Ayala Lasso, a former Ecuadorean U.N. envoy who was the first person to hold the post of U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights. He was appointed in 1994 but resigned in March this year to become his country's foreign minister.
Some U.N. members were unhappy that Ayala Lasso was not being succeeded by someone from the Third World, making it highly likely that Robinson's deputy would be from a developing country.

Robinson's early departure from the presidency means an election will have to be held in Ireland within 60 days after she leaves office. In the interim, a presidential commission will take over, comprising the chief justice of the supreme court and the presidents of the Dail (lower house of parliament) and the Senate.
